A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GraphJudge and its three-stage knowledge-graph construction framework. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark comparisons, module ablations, transfer experiments, graph-judgment evaluations, and appendix MCQ knowledge-retention results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and reports additional baseline, Windows-domain, transfer, and entity-coverage results.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain GPT-4o-mini extraction and denoising, supervised fine-tuning of the LLaMA-2-7B graph judge using positive and negative triples, and judgment-based filtering. The new entity-extraction prompt documents an existing step.

E1.justification: v4 adds evaluation on the Windows-centric Re-DocRED subset, extending coverage beyond Wikipedia and scientific abstracts to operating-system knowledge. Table 3 also expands transfer testing from GenWiki-to-REBEL-Sub alone to REBEL-Sub-to-GenWiki and REBEL-Sub-to-SCIERC, including a general-to-scientific domain shift.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated RAKG and iText2KG comparisons on all three retained datasets, expanding the baseline set from four to six. iText2KG was previously discussed but not evaluated there. Table 3 and the graph-judgment comparisons retain their existing comparator sets.

E3.justification: Existing training settings and graph metrics are retained. Added evaluations use REBEL-Sub-trained transfer models, the GenWiki-trained model for Re-DocRED, and entity-level BERTScore recall and accuracy. The MCQ-generation demonstration is revised between v3 Figure 10 and v4 Figure 12, without establishing that the retained MCQ results were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix E and Table 7 test entity coverage and accuracy before and after graph judgment, examining whether extraction supplies sufficient entities and filtering preserves coverage. Table 3 extends transfer robustness checks. Existing module ablations, denoising heatmaps, MCQ retention analysis, judge comparisons, and case study are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional experiments do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: All 15 retained Table 1 rows have identical values, but v4 adds substantial baseline, domain, transfer, and entity results. New Re-DocRED GraphJudge F1 scores are 0.7051/0.4322/0.3048 for G-BS/G-BL/G-RO. New transfer results are not uniformly best: on GenWiki, GraphJudge's G-RO-F1 is 0.5911 versus GPT-4o's 0.6028.

T1.justification: Definitions 1–2 and Equations 1–19 retain their mathematical content, with changes limited to notation spacing and typesetting. Neither version adds theoretical guarantees, formal assumptions, or proofs absent from the other.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about KG quality, state-of-the-art performance, and generalization. They still describe two general and one domain-specific dataset despite v4's expanded experimental coverage.

C2.justification: v4 interprets entity coverage as support for extraction and filtering, and newly attributes SCIERC transfer degradation to reduced in-domain training knowledge. That interpretation is metric-dependent: transfer improves G-BS-F1 from 0.7283 to 0.7431 relative to in-domain training, while BLEU and ROUGE F1 decline. Section 7's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 adds the entity-extraction template in Figure 10, baseline implementation guidance, and Re-DocRED subset/model provenance. It also revises the MCQ-generation example. Hardware, LoRA hyperparameters, and code-access information remain unchanged; Re-DocRED sample counts are not supplied.

R1.justification: v4 adds references for RAKG, LKD-KGC, Re-DocRED, and DocRED, plus newer hierarchical-RAG and recommendation applications. The related-work section and central novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes include localized wording edits, grouped citations, updated first-author affiliation and email, and insertion of Appendix E with subsequent appendix relabeling. The main section order and most explanatory prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains substantial comparison blocks, Table 3 becomes a full-width three-scenario table, and entity results receive a new Table 7. Several plots are restyled, while compact appendix prompt images become large boxed templates with an additional entity-extraction panel. Retained analyses and the case study are relocated or redisplayed.

improvement.justification: The added domain and transfer tests strengthen v3's narrow generalization evidence, while entity-coverage results and the missing extraction prompt improve methodological support and reproducibility. These gains are qualified by missing Re-DocRED sample counts, the overbroad SCIERC degradation explanation, and a newly invalid JSON options structure in the revised MCQ example.
